corrected.location: 9.74 + spurious chapter 10 'Book Three — Unity, Unity.' (10.0–10.10). Cut-off quotation only in original-en; modern-en/modern-da close it as 'UNITY, UNITY!' (two UNITYs, source has three)

results.evidence: original-en 9.74 ends 'easy as death is UNITY,'; chapter 10 'Book Three — Unity, Unity.' (11 paragraphs) exists in all editions, 18 chapters versus the source's 17. modern-en/da 9.74 close the quote as 'UNITY, UNITY!'. pg15837 lines 6473–6474 break the quotation before an all-caps line; Cornell and UC Irvine 1915 scans read 'UNITY, UNITY, UNITY.' inside 'The Loss of L'Univers'. SEO pages chapters.html and chapter-10.html also publish the spurious chapter.

All 17 listed paragraphs reproduce: 2,041 Howard words dropped, 311 replaced, net 1,730 (claim 1,734); 48 tail phrases give 0 hits in modern-en. The same pattern affects 34 more paragraphs, making 51, with 3,685 words dropped and net loss about 3,005. Replacement endings (e.g. 1.24 'reported it to the sheriff') appear in neither Howard nor Lagerlöf's Swedish (1905), and both match original-en. modern-da mirrors. original-en is verbatim Howard.

modern-en chapters 15–18 are byte-identical to original-en: 338/338 paragraphs, 16,179 words, equal chapter-array SHA-256. They keep PG typography (36 '--', 7 'to-day/to-morrow', 0 em dashes), while chapters 1–14 have 0 '--' and 113 em dashes. Content is complete (verbatim Howard) but served under the 'Modern English' label.

Body paragraphs 1.55 'II', 1.87 'III', 1.132 'IV', 1.307 'BOOK TWO' and 8.235 'BOOK THREE' appear in all three editions (modern-da 'ANDEN BOG', 'BOG TRE'). They are source headings at pg15837 lines 681, 817, 1046, 1679 and 6021; sub-numeral 'I' (line 291) is not served. The only correction is trivial: extent is 7 words, not 6.

modern-da chapter 3 ('Kapitel 3') is 87/87 paragraphs and 11,593 words byte-identical to original-en (equal SHA-256). Chapters 1–2 are Danish; chapter 3 is entirely English. modern-da 2.36 is Danish; 3.0 is English 'I looked at him, lost in astonishment.' original-en is verbatim PG #219 (Part III from line 2322). Standard Ebooks part-3 (87 paragraphs) matches served modern-da chapter 3 at 0.998 similarity. No Danish Part III exists in the edition.

modern-en chapter 1 'Mowgli's Brothers' is byte-identical to original-en: 154/154 paragraphs, 7,534 words, equal SHA-256, with PG '--' dashes retained. Every paragraph is verbatim in pg236 lines 56–856 with no uncovered source stretch. Standard Ebooks 'mowglis-brothers' matches at 0.9885 similarity. Content is complete but the 1894 text is served as 'Modern English' (hasAudio).

All editions begin 1.0 'I was born in Tuckahoe'. 'lions write history', 'In the month of August, 1841, I attended', 'NO COMPROMISE WITH SLAVERY' and 'Wendell Phillips' give 0 hits. pg23: Preface lines 84–373 (3,117 words), Phillips letter 378–486 (1,070). The Wellesley scan of the Boston 1845 printing places both before CHAPTER I. Neither is by Douglass, and the app's onboarding quotes both. The PG bio note is correctly excluded. Scope decision, S3.

Literal _…_ spans: 46 in original-en, 31 in modern-en, 28 in modern-da; no *…* spans. The classic reader (/read/…, /app) uses ParagraphRenderer.tsx, which converts only *…*/**…** (regex line 95), so underscores display; only the private lab reader (/reader, /lab) italicises _…_. Examples: 2.6 '_Great House Farm._' (all editions); 12.10 'LYNN, _Mass., April_ 28, 1845.' (original-en and modern-en; the modern-da 12.10 has none).

34.20 ends 'ten minutes before nine.[1]'. 34.22 is '[1] A somewhat remarkable eccentricity on the part of the London clocks!—TRANSLATOR.' in original-en and modern-en, and ends '— OVERSÆTTEREN.' in modern-da (11 words plus marker). pg103 (tr. George M. Towle) has the marker at line 7449 and the note at 7455–7456. The 1874 Sampson Low Towle scan has a note mark after 'nine.'; Standard Ebooks omits the note. It is translator apparatus served as body text.

new_observations.description: modern-en inserts or substitutes text found in neither Howard nor Lagerlöf's Swedish, and modern-da mirrors it. Examples: 1.10 adds 95 words ('trudging along a road toward a big farmstead… grain sacks'); 3.35 gives Big Ingmar 'two' children named Ingmar and Brita instead of the three rescued children; 4.6 changes why Karin breaks the engagement ('I cannot leave the farm' instead of Halvor's drunkenness at Falun); 6.60 swaps the speakers. Totals: 9+ insertions of 20+ words (about 400 words), invented endings in most of the 51 claim-02 paragraphs, and 10 same-length heavy rewrites.
The static SEO pages publish the spurious chapter 'Book Three — Unity, Unity.' (adjacent to G07-jerusalem-01).
Four of Douglass's own footnotes are served as body paragraphs, with inline [1]–[4] markers left in the text.
Appendix verse is served as run-on prose with no line breaks: 12.1 (Whittier, 104 words) and 12.7 ('A Parody', 414 words). The heading 'A PARODY' is served as body paragraph 12.6.
The PG placeholder '[Illustration: The “Cold Lairs”]' (pg236 line 1367) is served as a paragraph. It is arguably S3 as boilerplate mid-text.

Further byte-identical long prose paragraphs of 60+ words appear in modern-en: ch2 ×2, ch4 ×13 (1,121 words), ch5 ×9 (754 words), ch6 ×3, ch7 ×3. This may be intentional light-touch modernisation; it is not asserted as a defect.
